# Cascading Soft-Delete, Global Read Scoping and Archive Recovery (Ash Framework v3)

## Background

`/home/user/forum` holds a Mix project (OTP app `:forum`) for a discussion-forum backend built on the
Ash Framework v3 (`ash 3.31.0`). Content is three levels deep: a post owns comments, and a comment
owns reactions.

Deleting content in this product is never destructive: removed content stays in storage, stays
invisible to ordinary readers, can be inspected by an administrator, and can be recovered later.
Recovery has to be *precise* — undoing a deletion must bring back exactly what that deletion removed
and must not resurrect content that had already been deleted by an earlier, unrelated operation.

The project currently contains only the domain shell and the project configuration. Everything
described below is missing and must be built.

## Requirements

### Domain and resources

The domain module `Forum.Content` (`lib/forum/content.ex`) must expose exactly these three
resources, each using `Ash.DataLayer.Ets` configured with `private? true`:

| Module                   | File                            | Own attribute                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `Forum.Content.Post`     | `lib/forum/content/post.ex`     | `title` — `:string`, public, required |
| `Forum.Content.Comment`  | `lib/forum/content/comment.ex`  | `body` — `:string`, public, required  |
| `Forum.Content.Reaction` | `lib/forum/content/reaction.ex` | `emoji` — `:string`, public, required |

Every one of the three resources also has:

* a primary key attribute named `id` of type `:uuid`, generated by default;
* a public attribute `archived_at` of type `:utc_datetime_usec`, `nil` for live records;
* a public attribute `archive_batch_id` of type `:uuid`, `nil` for live records.

Relationships:

* `Forum.Content.Post` — a to-many relationship named `:comments` pointing at
  `Forum.Content.Comment`.
* `Forum.Content.Comment` — a to-one relationship named `:post` pointing at `Forum.Content.Post`,
  backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute `post_id`; and a to-many
  relationship named `:reactions` pointing at `Forum.Content.Reaction`.
* `Forum.Content.Reaction` — a to-one relationship named `:comment` pointing at
  `Forum.Content.Comment`, backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute
  `comment_id`.

Aggregates:

* `Forum.Content.Post` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `comment_count` over `:comments`.
* `Forum.Content.Comment` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `reaction_count` over
  `:reactions`.

### Actions

All three resources must define these seven actions under exactly these names:

| Name             | Action type                                           | Input                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:create`        | create                                                | the resource's own required attribute plus its foreign key (`post_id` for a comment, `comment_id` for a reaction) |
| `:read`          | read (**must be the resource's primary read action**) | none                                                                                                              |
| `:archived`      | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |
| `:with_archived` | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |
| `:archive`       | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |
| `:restore`       | update                                                | none                                                                                                              |
| `:purge`         | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |

"Input: none" is binding: each of those actions must succeed when invoked with an empty parameter
map and no additional arguments, e.g. `Ash.Query.for_read(Forum.Content.Post, :with_archived, %{})`,
`Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(record, :archive, %{})` and
`Ash.Changeset.for_update(record, :restore, %{})`.

### Archive semantics — action `:archive`

* Nothing is ever removed from storage by `:archive`.
* If the target record is already archived, the call still succeeds but nothing changes anywhere:
  the target keeps its existing `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id`, and no descendant is modified.
* Otherwise the target and every descendant of the target that is not already archived (a post's
  comments and those comments' reactions; a comment's reactions) are archived together as one
  generation: all of them end up with the *same* non-`nil` `archived_at` value and the *same*
  non-`nil` `archive_batch_id` value.
* Descendants that were already archived before the call keep their existing `archived_at` and
  `archive_batch_id` values byte-for-byte.
* Two separate archive operations must never produce the same `archive_batch_id`.

### Restore semantics — action `:restore`

* On a record that is not archived the call succeeds and changes nothing, anywhere.
* On an archived record: the target's `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` both become `nil`, and
  every descendant whose `archive_batch_id` equals the target's `archive_batch_id` as it was
  immediately before the call is restored the same way (`archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` set to
  `nil`), recursively.
* Descendants carrying a different `archive_batch_id` are left exactly as they were.
* `:restore` never affects ancestors of the target.

### Purge semantics — action `:purge`

* Invoked on a record whose `archived_at` is `nil`, the action must fail and change nothing: the
  result must be `{:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{errors: errors}}` where at least one element of
  `errors` is an `%Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges{}` whose `:fields` is `[:archived_at]` and whose
  `:message` is exactly `"must be archived before it can be purged"`.
* Invoked on an archived record, the record and every one of its descendants are permanently and
  irrecoverably removed from storage.

### Read scoping

* `:read` returns only records whose `archived_at` is `nil`. This scoping is global, not merely
  top-level: it must also hold everywhere a resource is reached indirectly — relationship loads
  (`Ash.load/3`), the `comment_count` and `reaction_count` aggregates, and filter expressions that
  traverse a relationship — so archived records can never leak into a result derived from an
  ordinary read.
* `:with_archived` returns both archived and live records.
* `:archived` returns only records whose `archived_at` is not `nil`.
* Fetching an archived record through the primary read (for example `Ash.get/3` with its default
  action) must produce an `Ash.Error.Query.NotFound`.

### Authorization

* All three resources must run `Ash.Policy.Authorizer`.
* An actor is a plain Elixir map. An actor is an administrator when its `:role` key equals `:admin`.
* With authorization enabled, the `:archived` read must be reachable only by an administrator.
  For any other actor, including `nil`, the call must return `{:error, %Ash.Error.Forbidden{}}` —
  not an empty result set.
* With authorization enabled, every other action on every resource must be permitted for every
  actor, including `nil`.

### Shared implementation modules

Three modules must be written once and shared, rather than duplicated per resource:

| Module                                    | File                                              | Behaviour                  | Must be referenced by                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Forum.Archive.Preparations.ArchiveScope` | `lib/forum/archive/preparations/archive_scope.ex` | `Ash.Resource.Preparation` | the `:read`, `:archived` and `:with_archived` actions of all three resources (directly on the action or through a resource-wide preparation) |
| `Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeArchive`    | `lib/forum/archive/changes/cascade_archive.ex`    | `Ash.Resource.Change`      | the `:archive` action of all three resources                                                                                                 |
| `Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeRestore`    | `lib/forum/archive/changes/cascade_restore.ex`    | `Ash.Resource.Change`      | the `:restore` action of all three resources                                                                                                 |

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: /home/user/forum
* The project must keep compiling as a standard Mix project: `mix compile` from
  `/home/user/forum` must succeed. Verification executes a standalone Elixir script from the
  project root with `mix run <script>` in the default `dev` Mix environment, so everything
  described above must be part of the ordinary `lib/` compilation of the `:forum` application.
* The machine has no network access. `ash 3.31.0` and `simple_sat` are already fetched and compiled
  for both the `dev` and `test` Mix environments. Do not add, remove or change dependencies in
  `mix.exs` or `mix.lock`.
* Keep `config/config.exs`'s `ash_domains: [Forum.Content]` entry intact and register all three
  resources in `Forum.Content`.
* Verification calls the actions through the plain `Ash` functions (`Ash.create/2`, `Ash.read/2`,
  `Ash.load/3`, `Ash.get/3`, `Ash.update/3`, `Ash.destroy/2`) with the action selected explicitly,
  and passes `authorize?: false` except where authorization itself is under test. Do not rely on
  domain code interfaces existing; add them only if you want them.
* Compiler warnings are tolerated; compilation errors are not.

defmodule Forum.Archive.Preparations.ArchiveScope do
  use Ash.Resource.Preparation

  @impl true
  def prepare(query, _opts, _context) do
    case query.action.name do
      :read ->
        Ash.Query.filter(query, is_nil(archived_at))

      :archived ->
        Ash.Query.filter(query, not(is_nil(archived_at)))

      :with_archived ->
        query

      _ ->
        query
    end
  end
end

      assert {:ok, [_]} =

               |> Ash.Query.for_read(:archived, %{})

               post
               |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
               |> Ash.update(actor: nil, authorize?: true)
    end
  end

    test "restoring a live record does nothing" do

      assert is_nil(post_restored.archive_batch_id)

      comment2_after = Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^comment2.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)

      assert {:ok, post} =

               |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
               |> Ash.update(actor: nil, authorize?: true)
    end
  end

defmodule ForumTest do
  use ExUnit.Case
  require Ash.Query

  alias Forum.Content.{Post, Comment, Reaction}

  setup do
    # Clear ETS tables if they exist
    if :ets.info(Post) != :undefined, do: :ets.delete_all_objects(Post)
    if :ets.info(Comment) != :undefined, do: :ets.delete_all_objects(Comment)
    if :ets.info(Reaction) != :undefined, do: :ets.delete_all_objects(Reaction)
    :ok
  end

  describe "basic creation and retrieval" do
    test "can create post, comment, and reaction" do
      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post 1"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      assert post.title == "Post 1"
      assert is_nil(post.archived_at)
      assert is_nil(post.archive_batch_id)

      comment = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment 1", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      assert comment.body == "Comment 1"
      assert comment.post_id == post.id

      reaction = Reaction |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "👍", comment_id: comment.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      assert reaction.emoji == "👍"
      assert reaction.comment_id == comment.id
    end
  end

  describe "read scoping and aggregates" do
    test "primary read action filters out archived records" do
      post1 = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Live Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      post2 = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Archived Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      # Archive post2
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(post2, action: :archive, authorize?: false)

      # Ordinary read
      live_posts = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:read, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
      assert length(live_posts) == 1
      assert hd(live_posts).id == post1.id

      # Archived read
      archived_posts = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:archived, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
      assert length(archived_posts) == 1
      assert hd(archived_posts).id == post2.id

      # With archived read
      all_posts = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
      assert length(all_posts) == 2

      # Ash.get/3 with default read should fail for archived post
      assert {:error, error} = Ash.get(Post, post2.id, authorize?: false)
      assert match?(%Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}, error) or
             (match?(%Ash.Error.Invalid{}, error) and Enum.any?(error.errors, &match?(%Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}, &1)))

      # Ash.get/3 with default read should succeed for live post
      assert Ash.get!(Post, post1.id, authorize?: false).id == post1.id
    end

    test "relationship loads and aggregates exclude archived records" do
      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      comment1 = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Live Comment", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      comment2 = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Archived Comment", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      # Archive comment2
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(comment2, action: :archive, authorize?: false)

      # Load comments on post
      post = Ash.load!(post, [:comments, :comment_count], authorize?: false)
      assert length(post.comments) == 1
      assert hd(post.comments).id == comment1.id
      assert post.comment_count == 1
    end
  end

  describe "archive semantics" do
    test "archiving a post cascades to comments and reactions" do
      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      comment = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      reaction = Reaction |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "👍", comment_id: comment.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      # Archive post
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(post, action: :archive, authorize?: false)

      # Fetch post, comment and reaction including archived
      post = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: post.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)
      assert not is_nil(post.archived_at)
      assert not is_nil(post.archive_batch_id)

      comment = Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: comment.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)
      reaction = Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: reaction.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)

      assert comment.archived_at == post.archived_at
      assert comment.archive_batch_id == post.archive_batch_id

      assert reaction.archived_at == post.archived_at
      assert reaction.archive_batch_id == post.archive_batch_id
    end

      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(post, action: :archive, authorize?: false)

      post = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: post.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)
      original_archived_at = post.archived_at
      original_batch_id = post.archive_batch_id

      post_again = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: post.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)
      assert post_again.archived_at == original_archived_at
      assert post_again.archive_batch_id == original_batch_id
    end

    test "does not modify already archived descendants" do

      comment1 = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment 1", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      assert comment1_after.archived_at == comment1.archived_at

    end
  end

      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      comment2 = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment 2", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      comment1_after = Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: comment1_archived.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)
      comment2_after = Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: comment2.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)

      # comment2 should be restored (same batch)
      assert is_nil(comment2_after.archived_at)
      assert is_nil(comment2_after.archive_batch_id)
    end
  end

  describe "purge semantics" do
    test "purging a live record fails with specific error" do
      post = Post |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Post"}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      assert {:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{errors: errors}} = Ash.destroy(post, action: :purge, authorize?: false)

      end)
    end

      comment = Comment |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment", post_id: post.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)
      _reaction = Reaction |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "👍", comment_id: comment.id}) |> Ash.create!(authorize?: false)

      # Archive post
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(post, action: :archive, authorize?: false)
      post_archived = Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id: post.id) |> Ash.read_one!(authorize?: false)

      # Purge post
      :ok = Ash.destroy!(post_archived, action: :purge, authorize?: false)

      # Verify all are gone from storage completely
      assert [] == Post |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
      assert [] == Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
      assert [] == Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.read!(authorize?: false)
    end
  end
